info.title: Encore
info.description:
Event ticketing, as a modular monolith. Five modules, and since the Payments extraction two hosts: Encore.Api serves everything here except the three /internal/payments routes, which only Encore.Payments.Api maps. Paths that carry their own `servers` entry are the ones the host serving this page does not answer.

**Actions, not resources.** The seat routes are `/hold`, `/release` and `/purchase` rather than a `/holds` collection: a hold is not an entity, it is two fields on the seat row, so it gets no URI of its own. All three are idempotent, which is what makes retrying a POST safe.

**Branch on `reason`, not on status.** Every refusal about the state of the world is `409` with a machine-readable `reason` and a `retriable` flag. Only an addressed thing that is not there is `404`. A request that is wrong on its own terms is `400`. The statuses carry the class of failure; `reason` carries which one.

**`X-Client-Id` is a claimed identity, not authentication.** Anyone can change it and reset their own hold cap. It stands in for the Identity module, which does not exist yet, which is also why no customer route returns 401 or 403. Only the three /internal/payments routes answer 401, when the service token is wrong.

This document is hand-maintained. `Encore.Api` holds zero NuGet packages by design, so nothing generates this from endpoint metadata. Tests fail when it and the mapped routes disagree, and when a documented status enum and the enum behind it disagree.

servers.description: Whichever instance served this page — 5107 from dotnet run, 8080 from the container.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness, and readiness. Both hosts serve both routes.

tags.name: catalog
tags.description: Venues and events. Read-mostly CRUD, public, no client identity.

tags.name: inventory
tags.description: Seats. The contended module: hold, release, purchase.

tags.name: orders
tags.description: Checkout. Prices through Catalog, holds through Inventory, charges through Payments.

tags.name: payments
tags.description: Read-only. Orders drives payment, because Orders knows what is owed.

tags.name: payments-service
tags.description: Service-to-service only. Orders calls these when Payments runs as its own process; no customer can reach them.

ClientId.name: X-Client-Id
ClientId.description: A GUID identifying the calling client. NOT authentication — it is unverified and anyone may change it. Paste any GUID here to try the seat, order and payment routes.

ServiceToken.name: X-Service-Token
ServiceToken.description: The shared secret between Orders and Payments. This one IS authentication, and it is the only thing guarding a call that can move money. Not a customer credential — the /internal routes take no X-Client-Id at all.

ReadinessResponse.description: One entry per module that registered a readiness check. A module is free to be ready while reporting something it wants looked at — a dead letter does not take a host out of rotation.

detail.description: One line for a human, and where the counts live.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Module refusals add `reason` and `retriable`; framework refusals (404 for an unmatched route, 405, 415, a body that will not bind) carry only the standard members.

reason.description: Machine-readable refusal code. Branch on this.

retriable.description: Whether trying again could succeed: later, or after a new hold or a different card.

orderId.description: Present on checkout_already_open: the open checkout, so a client whose 201 was lost can confirm or cancel it. Null only if it closed in between.

seats.description: Present on seats_unavailable: every seat that could not be held.

reason.description: already_held, already_sold, seat_not_found, hold_cap_reached, concurrent_request_in_flight or lost_race.

startsAt.description: Must carry a timezone. Stored and returned as UTC.

onSaleAt.description: When tickets become orderable. Null means immediately. Must carry a timezone when supplied.

price.description: What one seat costs. At most 4 decimal places; more is refused, not rounded.

holdExpiresAt.description: Five minutes out. The duration is owned by the domain; a caller never supplies it.

seatIds.description: At most four, the per-client hold cap. A repeated id is refused, not de-duplicated.

status.description: awaiting_capture is non-terminal: every seat is sold and the capture is owed. The next confirm resolves it, and so does the capture sweep, within a minute or two.
abandoned: the reconciler found no record at the gateway, so the attempt never arrived and the order may be paid for again.

AuthorizeAttemptRequest.description: What Orders sends to open or reuse an authorisation. The client id is in the body rather than a header: the caller is Orders reporting a fact about the order, not a customer asserting who it is.

OrderAttemptRequest.description: Keyed by order rather than by payment, because IOrderPayments is: the module owns which attempt an order currently means, and the one-live-attempt index picks it out.

PaymentOutcomeResponse.description: A successful service call. Branch on `outcome`, never on the status code — several statuses share a code, and the string is the half that is one-to-one with the contract vocabulary.

BadClientId.description: The X-Client-Id header is missing or is not a GUID. No `reason`: the request is malformed rather than refused.

BadServiceToken.description: The X-Service-Token header is missing, malformed or wrong. One refusal for all three, with `reason` service_token_invalid: telling an unauthenticated caller which of those it got tells it how to get closer.

get.description: The host's own route, not a framework health check. A 200 means the pipeline is serving and the migrators have finished, because they run as IHostedLifecycleService before Kestrel opens the socket.

Asks every module that registered an IReadinessCheck whether it can work, and reports the answers together. 200 when all of them can, 503 when any cannot. The host itself knows none of this — it counts votes, because it is not allowed to know that a module has a database. The detail lines carry the numbers worth watching rather than alerting on: dead-lettered outbox messages, and timed-out payment attempts the reconciler has not settled. Both hosts serve this route.

503.description: At least one module cannot work. The body says which, and why.

post.summary: Creates a venue and returns it.
post.description: Operator-facing. Ids are generated here, not supplied.

post.summary: Creates an event at an existing venue and returns it.

400.description: reason: invalid_name, invalid_price, invalid_currency, ambiguous_timestamp. The last one is a startsAt or onSaleAt with no timezone.

409.description: reason: venue_not_found. Create the venue before the event.

post.summary: Creates an event's seats and returns their ids.
post.description: Operator-facing, and the only seat route with no client identity: creating a seat map is not something a customer does. Returns 201 with no Location header, because there is no GET for a seat map and a Location pointing at nothing is worse than none. Not safe to retry, unlike the seat actions: each call adds a fresh set of seats.

400.description: An empty event id, or a count outside 1..10000. No `reason` member on this one.

post.summary: Holds a seat for the calling client for five minutes.
post.description: Idempotent: the same client re-holding gets the same expiry back and raises no second event. A seat whose hold has lapsed is available again on this path whatever the stored status says, so an expired hold is reclaimed here rather than by waiting for a sweep.

404.description: reason: seat_not_found. Also the answer for a seat that exists under a different event, so seat ids cannot be discovered by asking.

409.description: reason: already_held (retriable), already_sold (not), hold_cap_reached (retriable, carries `limit`), lost_race (retriable), concurrent_request_in_flight (retriable).

post.description: Only the holding client may release. Releasing a seat that is already available is a no-op success.

409.description: reason: already_sold (sold to somebody else; terminal), sold_to_you (you bought it; terminal), not_the_holder, lost_race.

post.summary: Converts the calling client's live hold into a sale.
post.description: Requires a live, unexpired hold by the same client. There is no selling an available seat outright. Idempotent: re-buying a seat you already own returns 200.

409.description: reason: already_sold, not_the_holder, hold_expired (retriable), no_active_hold (retriable), lost_race (retriable).

post.summary: Opens a checkout: prices the event, holds every seat, returns the order.
post.description: A partial checkout writes nothing and releases nothing it did not take. One open checkout per client per event, enforced by a partial unique index rather than by a read-then-write.

400.description: Missing or malformed X-Client-Id, or reason: no_seats, too_many_seats (carries `limit`), duplicate_seat.

409.description: reason: event_not_found, not_on_sale, checkout_already_open (carries `orderId`), seats_unavailable (carries `seats`, each with its own reason: already_held, already_sold, seat_not_found, hold_cap_reached, concurrent_request_in_flight or lost_race).

get.summary: Reads one of the calling client's orders.
get.description: Another client's order is 404, not 403 — there is no authorisation system to produce a 403.

post.summary: Authorises the total, sells the seats, then captures.
post.description: In that order, because a sold seat is terminal and money is the one of the two that can be given back. Any path that does not end in every seat sold voids the authorisation, so a customer is never charged for an order they did not get. The sale is recorded as awaiting_capture before the capture is asked for; a capture that gets no answer leaves it there, and the next confirm or the capture sweep resolves it.

200.description: Confirmed. Re-confirming a confirmed order returns it unchanged.

409.description: reason: order_not_pending, holds_expired, payment_declined (retriable), payment_timed_out (retriable), order_failed, lost_race (retriable).

post.summary: Ends the order because the customer said so, releasing the seats.
post.description: The seats go back first and the money second. If a confirm of the same order has already sold the seats, nothing is released or voided: the answer is order_not_pending once that confirm has recorded the sale, or lost_race in the moment before it does, and the retry finds the order awaiting capture or confirmed.

409.description: reason: order_not_pending (a confirmed order cannot be changed), lost_race (retriable; a confirm got there first).

get.summary: Reads back what happened to a payment.
Lists the attempts against one order.
get.description: Read-only on purpose: Orders drives payment, because Orders is the thing that knows what is owed. There is no POST here.

200.description: Every attempt against that order, including superseded ones.

servers.description: payments-api. The monolith that serves this page does NOT map this route: MapPaymentsServiceApi is called only by Encore.Payments.Api.

post.summary: Opens or reuses this order's authorisation.
post.description: Idempotent per order: a repeat for an order that already has a live attempt returns that attempt rather than opening a second one, which is what makes a retry after a dropped response safe. Requires X-Service-Token; carries no X-Client-Id.

504.description: timed_out. The attempt is recorded and the reconciler will settle it.

servers.description: payments-api. The monolith that serves this page does NOT map this route: MapPaymentsServiceApi is called only by Encore.Payments.Api.

post.summary: Takes the funds this order's attempt is holding.
post.description: Idempotent: capturing an already-captured attempt answers captured rather than failing.

504.description: timed_out. The order is left awaiting capture and the next confirm resolves it.

servers.description: payments-api. The monolith that serves this page does NOT map this route: MapPaymentsServiceApi is called only by Encore.Payments.Api.

post.summary: Releases what this order's attempt is holding.
post.description: Idempotent: voiding an already-voided attempt answers no_authorization rather than failing. A captured attempt refuses, because the money has already moved.
